articles.title: Lawsuits Can’t Restrain Big Tech
articles.author: Rob Larson
articles.content_excerpt: When the government first filed major antitrust lawsuits targeting Big Tech back in 2020, many people were optimistic that the long-standing practice of public legal action against monopolistic companies could rein in these economy-dominating corporations. But as these pages have covered , this “techlash” has come to little. Antitrust law has conformed to its castrated character of recent decades, with the state unable to bring itself to seriously restrain, let alone break up, the giant companies even after they were ruled to be full monopolies just months before. articles.title: Evangelicals’ 10 Lessons in Leader Development for the Left
articles.author: Eric Blanc
articles.content_excerpt: Last week , I looked at what Rick Warren’s 1995 classic The Purpose Driven Church can teach the Left about recruitment in our atomized era. But getting people through the door is only half the battle. Seeker-sensitive evangelicalism didn’t buck America’s decades-long decline in membership organizations simply by attracting crowds. It couldn’t have grown without systematically turning newcomers into members, members into leaders, and leaders into recruiters. As Warren puts it, “Our ultimate goal at Saddleback is to turn an audience into an army.” This is where the Left is weakest. Radical and progressive organizations generally lose most people we bring in and develop only a fraction of the rest into organizers able and willing to recruit those around them. articles.author: Aaron Miguel Cantú
articles.content_excerpt: The opinions expressed here are solely the author's and do not reflect the opinions or beliefs of the LA Progressive. Big Tech companies and California’s largest oil and gas well operator are spending millions to pass a ballot measure that would clear hurdles for industrial projects such as gas pipelines and possibly data centers. Proposition 45 would alter the California Environmental Quality Act, known as CEQA, which requires often time-consuming reviews and public input for infrastructure and other construction projects. Those requirements would be clipped if voters pass the proposition in November, making projects harder to stop or delay. articles.author: Justin Mayhugh
articles.content_excerpt: The nurses and providers who care for our members at Ford plants across the country are now joining UAW themselves. They are the first physician assistant to be added to the Ford Salaried Agreement. Plant nurses are also salaried employees. articles.title: The Creativity Con Ate the Middle Class
articles.author: Thomas Frank
articles.content_excerpt: The faiths and hopes of the postwar middle-class society have mostly evaporated today. Our parents’ beliefs in consensus and the goodness of American civilization have joined mainline Protestantism and the benevolent corporation on some nostalgia channel of discarded ideas. One signature ideal of that era has survived, however. Indeed, it thrives; it glows with an incandescence that time cannot dim. I am referring to our ongoing fascination with creativity, the human power that our affluent-society ancestors liked to believe made life worth living and that was, at the same time, responsible for the forward motion of civilization itself. Every year brings a bumper crop of sunny new literature on this tired old subject. Self-help books tell us how to sharpen our skills and be more creative;

articles.author: Eileen Jones

articles.title: We Can Beat the Right With a Left-Wing Affordability Agenda
articles.author: Niko Block
articles.content_excerpt: In the past decade, much ink has been spilled over the question of whether we are witnessing a resurgence of fascism. Those debates have calmed since last November, when Donald Trump casually identified himself as a fascist amid a disorientingly effusive meeting with New York City’s Mayor-elect Zohran Mamdani. Part of the problem with the debate is that fascism can be difficult to define and identify — a point economist Isabella Weber makes at the outset of her new book, Anti-Fascist Economics . Unlike other major political ideologies, fascism has few defining texts, social theories, or economic platforms. articles.title: Peter Thomas Was a Marxist Intellectual With a Mission
articles.author: Max Tomba
articles.content_excerpt: It is difficult to write in memory of Peter Thomas. Not for lack of memories, but because there are too many. So many discussions come to mind, shared projects, collective volumes to which we both contributed. One obvious one is In Marx’s Laboratory: Critical Interpretations of the Grundrisse (2013), which Peter coedited with Riccardo Bellofiore and Guido Starosta. But my thoughts turn even more insistently to The Government of Time: Theories of Plural Temporality in the Marxist Tradition (2017), coedited by Peter and Vittorio Morfino. The preparation of that volume was accompanied by countless discussions and meetings. I remember one in Milan, intellectually lively, friendly, and full of good humor. articles.title: Equal Justice on the Road
articles.author: Sejal Desai
articles.content_excerpt: The opinions expressed here are solely the author's and do not reflect the opinions or beliefs of the LA Progressive. Every day, millions of people get behind the wheel trusting that others on the road will follow the rules. Most of the time, that trust holds. When it breaks, the results can change a life in seconds. A careless driver who runs a red light or checks a phone at the wrong moment can leave someone with injuries, medical bills, and months of lost income. In a large and busy city like Houston, where long commutes and crowded freeways are part of daily life, these moments happen far too often. A demonstration ends with a completed spreadsheet or a working piece of software. The discussion immediately moves to how many people will lose their jobs. Concern about GPT-6 Astra and jobs deserves a more careful answer than that leap allows: which work has been demonstrated, under what conditions, and what would have to change before an employer could rely on it? There are several decisions between completing a task and eliminating a position.
